title: Example 15-1: Poetic Rhyme Scheme within Body of Text

illustrates.quote: Paragraph Format. Follow print for spacing and capitalization when a rhyme scheme is indicated by a linear sequence of lowercase letters within the narrative body of text. Retain font attributes used for rhyme scheme letters. The rhyme scheme letter should be on a line with at least one word of the material to which it applies.

blocks.text: The rhyme scheme in these lines of Yeats *Resurrection* is abba. I saw a staring virgin stand *a* / Where holy Dionysus died, *b* / And tear the heart out of his side, *b* / And lay the heart upon her hand *a*
blocks.features: Ordinary running prose (15.7.1's own 'Paragraph Format'), quoting four lines of verse inline with a '/' marking each original print line break and an italic single letter after each quoted line naming its rhyme (markup DSL '*...*' = italic, per Emboss/format/cell-markup.mjs, the same convention every other gold section uses for emphasis in print.blocks text). 'continuation:true' because the given braille begins flush at cell 1 with no paragraph indent — this excerpt continues directly from the rule's own preceding sentence, not a fresh paragraph. Not poetry-formatted braille — no <poem>/<line> structure, no linenum apparatus; this rule is entirely about retaining print's own font attribute on the letters, unrelated to the linenum findings (F-181/F-182/F-205) that govern every other file in this section.

The prose sentence and all five rhyme letters/positions verify EXACTLY: 'The rhyme scheme in these lines of Yeats ' -> ',! rhyme s*eme 9 ^! l9es ( ,y1ts' (NO possessive apostrophe — confirmed by forward-translation: 'Yeats'' with an apostrophe would add a trailing dot-3 the source does not have), an italic 'Resurrection' -> '.1,resurrec;n' (byte-for-byte), each italic rhyme letter 'a'/'b' -> '.2a'/'.2;b' (byte-for-byte, confirmed with Emboss's own typeform array convention, one italic-typeform code point per input character). One detail remains UNVERIFIED: plain (non-italic) 'abba' translates through uebG2 as contracted 'a2a' (the one-cell 'bb' sign), not literally as four separate letter cells 'abba' the way the source's braille reads; several candidate markups (grade-1 word/passage wrapping, each letter individually italicised, space- or hyphen-separated) were tried and none reproduced the source's literal 'abba4' exactly — see compare-gold-15/differences.md for the attempts. Recorded as an unresolved micro-detail in 'uncertain' below rather than guessed; it affects only this one four-letter word, not the sentence's structure or any other file.
